content.text: {"headline":"Approve P0 (No action): predicted 82.0% service level for 17:30-20:00 against the 80% target, at no extra cost. General is still forecast below target at 76.4%.","why":"P0 is the cheapest plan that follows policy and reaches the target over the 17:30-20:00 disruption window. Predicted service level is 82.0% overall, with payments at 87.9% and abandons at 4.0%, for ₹0. The campaign email (MKT-2026-556) pushed general calls 20–45% over forecast, led by new_offer_enquiry at 2.74x normal. Payments has a separate problem: it is about 4 agents short because of sickness. Both queues are predicted to recover by the evening window without intervention. No escalation is flagged.","trade_offs":["The general queue stays below target under P0 at 76.4%. P2 is the only option shown that lifts general above target, to 81.6%, and it raises overall service level to 84.2% and cuts abandons to 3.0%, for ₹240.","P1 also costs ₹0 but does worse than doing nothing: 80.5% overall, general 75.2%, and payments drops to 86.1% because 3 cross-skilled agents are lent away from it.","P3 has the same predicted outcome and cost as P2 (84.2%, ₹240) but also uses the last overtime budget. It gains nothing over P2 and leaves no reserve.","Moving agents out of payments (P1–P3) lowers its service level slightly, by 1.1–1.8 points, while it is already short-staffed."],"watch":"Watch general service level and new_offer_enquiry volume. The 82.0% prediction leaves only 2 points of margin, and general is already forecast at 76.4%. If campaign calls keep running over forecast, or payments sickness worsens, switch to P2 (₹240), the cheapest option shown that lifts general above target."}
